Duties include but not limited to: Functions as liaison and is responsible for planning, coordinating, and performing a wide range of clinical, administrative , program, and technical functions to support quality case manage of sex specific services for veterans.

Works directly, with the patients, VA staff, non-VA care provides and organizations, Radiology Departments, and the Women Veterans Program Manager to achieve seamless care, facilitate patient satisfaction, reduce duplication of services or delay of care, and monitor quality of care and services received.

Responsible and accountable for the provision of direct and indirect care and for the delivery of quality nursing care to a culturally Veteran population. Provides care and counseling of persons to promote and maintain health.

Coordinating and tracking sex specific care (i.e., breast care/mammography, gynecological coordination, maternity care, etc.) of patients throughout all aspects of the medical center, including Community Based Outpatient Clinics, as well as community vendors and or agencies.

Assists with initial VA consult referrals for gynecology, mammography, non-VA care, and/or other care assisting with VA or community services for the patient with an appropriate provider, to include coordinating any subsequent appointments or follow ups, as needed.

Educates patients on a variety of sex specific topics, to include importance of routine medical screenings. Assists veterans who have presented to VA or non VA emergency department for gender specific emergencies, to secure appropriate follow up care such as a lab, ultrasound, emotional support, and/or other care as needed.

Coordinates care with the Veterans Patient Aligned Care Team (PACT). Documents patient care interactions accurately, succinctly, and timely, using appropriate notes, templates, and clinical reminders, in the electronic medical record.

Manages appropriate use of the electronic alert (flag) for breast breast and cervical screenings, and/or other issues in the electronic medical record. Understands and responds to mammography reports, BIRADS, Pap and other sex specific screening/diagnostic test results. Documents communication of the test results for female specific testing.

Contacts patients who fail to keep mammogram appointments, or who are delinquent in obtaining recommended breast cancer or other diagnostic screenings (i.e., Pap), to determine and resolve obstacles the veteran may have with keeping appointments.

Participates in quality improvement programs and initiatives including system redesign, to improve access, quality efficiency, and patient satisfaction.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: 0800-16:30, Monday - Friday.

Compressed/Flexible: Not available. Telework: Ad-hoc. Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized. Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized.
Basic Requirements: United States Citizenship: Non-citizens may only be appointed when it is not possible to recruit qualified citizens in accordance with VA Policy. English Language Proficiency.

In accordance with 38 U.S.C. 7403(f), no person shall serve in direct patient care positions unless they are proficient in basic written and spoken English.

Graduate of a school of professional nursing approved by the appropriate accrediting agency and accredited by one of the following accrediting bodies at the time the program was completed by the applicant: The Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE); OR Individuals attending a master's level bridge program in nursing who have completed coursework equivalent to a bachelor's level degree in Nursing may have opportunity to become registered as a nurse with a state licensing board prior to completion of the bridge program.

Upon achievement of a State license, the individual may be appointed on temporary basis and later converted to a permanent appointment upon successful completion and graduation from the bridge program.

(Reference VA Handbook 5005, Appendix G6); OR In cases of graduates of foreign schools of professional nursing, possession of a current, full, active, and unrestricted registration will meet the requirement for graduation from an approved school of professional nursing to warrant an appointment as a Nurse who has completed an associated degree/entry level Nursing education program.

Nurse I, Level II Demonstrates integration of biopsychosocial concepts, cognitive skills and technically competent practice in providing care to clients with basic or complex.

An ADN or Diploma in Nursing AND 1 year of specialized nursing experience equivalent to Nurse I, Level 1 ;OR a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) with no additional professional nursing experience required. Self-directed in goal setting for managing complex client situations.

An ADN or Diploma in Nursing AND 2 years of professional nursing experience in which one year is equivalent to Nurse I, Level 2; OR a BSN and 1 year of professional nursing experience equivalent to the Nurse I, Level 2; OR a Master's degree in nursing (MSN) and no additional professional nursing experience; OR a Master's degree in a *related field with a BSN and no additional professional nursing experience.

Nurse III Executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience and creative approaches to management of complex client care beyond the immediate practice setting.

Preferred Experience: 3-5 years of Women's Healthcare to include sex specific procedures, testing and evaluations. 3-5 years working as a Registered Nurse Case Manager. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/.

Physical Requirements: This position may include a level of physicality normally associated with duties performed by nursing personnel such as direct patient care, and potentially long periods of walking, standing, sitting, moderate lifting, repeated bending, or kneeling. Examples may include: Significant amounts of time standing assisting Veterans.

Utilization of safe patient handling and mobility protocols.

The Nurse- Nursing Officer of the Day (NOD) Registered Nurse (RN) directs position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to the management of complex patient care.

The NOD demonstrates the ability to plan and organize the delivery of care to assure continuity of care and peer accountability for practice, including access to care and discharge planning.

The NOD is skilled in the delivery of patient care and serves as the facility nursing expert at all hours to support, provide and facilitate emergency medical support throughout the facility.

The incumbent serves as the facility expert for all patient care areas in identifying escalating medical crises, environmental factors, and in allocating staffing resources appropriately throughout the facility to meet the care needs of Veterans.

The NOD uses clinical knowledge and judgment to promote staff involvement in planning, decision-making, and evaluating outcomes. They function proficiently in clinical practice and/or areas related to the assigned roles and responsibilities.

Evaluates current practice and formulates outcomes for groups of patients and/or organizational processes within an area of expertise. Guides, develops, and supports staff from a leadership perspective using professional standards of care, scientific evidence, and practice to evaluate programs and/or service activities.

The NOD is a skilled nurse who demonstrates advanced leadership at the systems level that is sustainable, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex situations. Other duties as assigned.

Assistant Nurse Manager - Community Living Center The Assistant Nurse Manager (CLC) is a self-directed nurse leader accountable to the Nursing Manager, ensuring resident-centered nursing care, staff supervision, and compliance with clinical and administrative standards.

Key Duties and Responsibilities Leadership & Oversight: Works under the Nursing Manager to ensure the 24/7 operation of the unit, providing timely, high-quality nursing care that meets accepted clinical standards.

Nursing Standards: Develops and implements nursing standards for specific resident populations in long-term care, ensuring compliance with ethical and privacy requirements. Staff Management: Plans and prioritizes work, assigns tasks based on staff capabilities, evaluates performance, provides counseling, and resolves complaints.

Recruitment & Training: Assists with interviews, selection, and hiring new staff; identifies training needs and arranges development opportunities. Regulatory Compliance: Maintains accreditation readiness, supports performance measures and ensures adherence to federal/state regulations.

Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Leads interdisciplinary groups to build relationships with professional and health-related organizations. Quality & Safety: Implements quality improvement initiatives, medication safety protocols, and patient care standards.

· Für ein bekanntes Haus im Bereich Pflege und Medizin in der Region Oberriet suchen wir Sie als Dipl. Experte/-in Anästhesiepflege NDS.
### Dipl. Experte/-in Anästhesiepflege NDS in Oberriet – die Eckdaten Ihrer Stelle
**Position:** Dipl. Experte/-in Anästhesiepflege NDS
**Fachbereich:** Gesundheitswesen
**Pensum:** Nach Vereinbarung
**Anstellung:** Temporäreinsatz
**Start:** Nach Vereinbarung
**Arbeitsort:** Region Oberriet
**Arbeitgeber:** Den Namen nennen wir Ihnen gerne im Gespräch
Kurz gesagt: Der Rahmen stimmt. Zudem lernen Sie nun den Arbeitsort besser kennen, denn genau darum geht es als Nächstes.
Oberriet liegt in der Nähe von Altstätten im östlichen Kanton St. Gallen und ist verkehrstechnisch sehr gut erschlossen. Die Region profitiert von der Nähe zur Liechtenstein und verfügt über gute Zuganbindungen ins Rheintal. Als Arbeitsort ist Oberriet attraktiv, da Sie hier von einem vielfältigen Wirtschaftsangebot, kurzen Pendlerwegen und einer hohen Lebensqualität profitieren. Die unmittelbare Nähe zur Natur ergänzt das attraktive Arbeitsumfeld ideal.
### Das packen Sie als Anästhesiepflege in Oberriet an
· Zuerst bereiten Sie die Narkose vor, dazu Medikamente und Geräte
· Dabei lückenlose Überwachung von Kreislauf, Atmung und Narkosetiefe
· Ebenso assistieren Sie bei Ein- und Ausleitung, Seite an Seite mit der Ärztin
· Zudem sichere Übergabe in den Aufwachraum mit klarer Dokumentation
· Dazu souveränes Handeln bei Notfällen, denn Ruhe rettet Leben
· Ausserdem Mitverantwortung für Hygiene und Gerätechecks im OP
### Ihr Rüstzeug für den erfolgreichen Einstieg
· Zuerst das Fachliche: das NDS HF Anästhesiepflege auf dem Pflegediplom
· Bei ausländischem Abschluss: SRK-Anerkennung erforderlich
· Vor allem Präzision, Ruhe sowie schnelle Auffassung im Ernstfall
· Zudem Teamgeist, denn im OP zählt jedes Zahnrad
· Bereitschaft zu Diensten gemäss OP-Programm
### Ihr Arbeitsumfeld: Ihre neue Wirkungsstätte
Sie arbeiten in einem etablierten Haus der Pflege – mit einem eingespielten Team, klaren Abläufen und echter Wertschätzung. Dabei erwartet Sie ein Umfeld, in dem Fachlichkeit und Menschlichkeit zusammengehören.
Kurz gesagt: Als Anästhesiepflege in Oberriet verbinden Sie Fachlichkeit mit einem Umfeld, das zu Ihnen passt. Genau solche Stellen vermitteln wir am liebsten.
### Der Beruf im Detail: Was macht eine diplomierte Expertin Anästhesiepflege NDS?
Dipl. Expertinnen und Experten Anästhesiepflege NDS arbeiten dort, wo Sekunden zählen. Zuerst bereiten Sie Narkosen vor, dann überwachen Sie Kreislauf und Atmung während des Eingriffs und begleiten Patientinnen sicher in den Aufwachraum. Dabei arbeiten Sie Seite an Seite mit der Anästhesieärztin – ein eingespieltes Duo im Operationssaal.
Voraussetzung ist das Nachdiplomstudium NDS HF Anästhesiepflege auf dem Pflegediplom. Somit vereint dieser Beruf Hightech-Medizin, Präzision und echte Verantwortung – und wird entsprechend gesucht und geschätzt.
Die Region Oberriet verzeichnet eine hohe Nachfrage nach diplomierten Experten und Expertinnen für Anästhesiepflege, da Spitäler und Kliniken verstärkt spezialisierte Fachkräfte suchen. Sie profitieren von ausgezeichneten Karrierechancen und flexiblen Pensumsmodellen, die Ihre Work-Life-Balance berücksichtigen. iPersonal unterstützt Sie als erfahrener Vermittler mit gezielter Platzierung und umfassender Begleitung beim erfolgreichen Berufsstart.
### Ihre Vorteile mit MediPersonal in der Region Oberriet
· Gratis-Weiterbildungen dank [Temptraining](https://temptraining.ch) – denn wir fördern Ihre Karriere aktiv
· Eine feste Beraterin begleitet Sie persönlich, von der Bewerbung bis zum ersten Tag
· Dazu schnelle sowie ehrliche Antworten – meist innerhalb von 24 Stunden
· Faire Verträge nach GAV, denn Ihr Lohn soll klar und offen sein
· Zudem eine langfristige Perspektive, denn wir vermitteln Stellen, die wirklich zu Ihrem Leben passen
· Und vor allem: Diskretion garantiert – Ihre Bewerbung behandeln wir streng vertraulich
### Häufige Fragen zur Stelle als Anästhesiepflege in Oberriet
**Welche Ausbildung brauche ich für die Anästhesiepflege?**
Dafür benötigen Sie das NDS HF Anästhesiepflege auf Ihrem Pflegediplom. Ausländische Abschlüsse brauchen zudem die SRK-Anerkennung.
**Arbeite ich im OP selbstständig?**
Sie arbeiten eigenständig in Ihrem Kompetenzbereich – und immer Seite an Seite mit der Anästhesieärztin. Denn im OP zählt das eingespielte Team.
**Wie schnell erhalte ich eine Rückmeldung auf meine Bewerbung?**
Meist hören Sie schon innerhalb von 24 Stunden von uns, denn Ihre Zeit ist uns wichtig. Zudem halten wir Sie danach laufend auf dem neusten Stand.

Ja, selbstverständlich – denn im persönlichen Gespräch nennen wir Ihnen die Institution gerne. Denn Offenheit gehört bei uns dazu.

## Dipl. Pflegefachfrau Pflegefachmann FH Schötz – Pflege ist mehr als nur ein Beruf
Du arbeitest als Dipl. Pflegefachfrau oder Pflegefachmann FH Schötz, und du spürst jeden Tag, dass Pflege mehr ist als ein Job. Als Dipl Pflegefachfrau Pflegefachmann FH Schötz setzt du dich für das Wohl der Menschen ein. Du hilfst Menschen in wichtigen Momenten, und gleichzeitig gibst du Sicherheit, sodass Vertrauen entsteht und Hoffnung wächst.
Schötz liegt im Kanton Luzern in der Schweiz und besticht durch seine zentrale Lage in der Zentralschweiz mit ausgezeichneter Verkehrsanbindung via Bahn und Autobahn. Sie profitieren von der Nähe zu Luzern und Zug, was kurze Pendlerwege ermöglicht. Die Region bietet eine attraktive Mischung aus ländlichem Charakter und wirtschaftlicher Dynamik, wodurch sich Schötz als zukunftsorientierter Arbeitsort etabliert hat.
Du begleitest Patientinnen und Patienten durch schwierige Zeiten, und du bist oft die Person, die Halt gibt. Genau deshalb ist Pflege nicht nur Arbeit, sondern auch eine echte Berufung, die Verantwortung und Menschlichkeit verbindet.
Einsatzort: Schötz und UmgebungEinsatzbeginn: Ab sofort oder nach Vereinbarung

Ihre Aufgabe
Der Schwerpunkt Ihrer Tätigkeit liegt in der Nachtwache. Während der Nacht sorgen Sie für Präsenz, Sicherheit und einen verlässlichen Rahmen im Haus. Sie sind Ansprechperson für unsere Bewohner und reagieren auch in ausserordentlichen oder anspruchsvollen Situationen ruhig, umsichtig und gemäss den internen Vorgaben.
Von 24.00 bis 06.00 Uhr ist eine Pikettschlafzeit vorgesehen. Während dieser Zeit können Sie vor Ort schlafen und bleiben für notwendige Einsätze erreichbar.

* 5-7 Nachtwachen pro Monat von 21.00 bis 09.00 Uhr
* 1-2 Tageseinsätze pro Monat von 09.00 bis 15.00 Uhr oder von 15.00 Uhr bis 21.00 Uhr
* Einsätze gemäss Dienstplan, teilweise auch an Wochenenden und Feiertagen
Ergänzend zur Nachtwache übernehmen Sie einzelne Einsätze im Tagesdienst. Dadurch lernen Sie unsere Bewohner:innen, den Alltag im Forelhaus und das Team auch ausserhalb der Nacht besser kennen. Dies schafft Kontinuität, stärkt die Zusammenarbeit und erleichtert den Informationsfluss zwischen Nacht- und Tagesbetrieb.

Participates in preventive health activities with local team; provides primary prevention activities regarding domestic violence/intimate partner violence in local schools; conducts in-service education for nursing and medical staff regarding forensic medical evidence collection; consults with the local law enforcement and prosecutor office regarding medical related issues and forensic evidence.

Assists nursing team care coordinators with all subspecialty clinics and in the Emergency Department; provides specialized health education to DV/IPV victims with special health care needs; organizes and coordinates multidisciplinary care conferences on medically complex and high-risk patients.

Plans program expansion to provide a Pediatric Sexual Assault/Abuse program. Assists with patient care in the Emergency Department, utilizes the nursing process and provides skilled and comprehensive nursing care to patients.

The Registered Nurse-PACT position is based in Primary Care at the Providence campus. This position is full time at 40 hours per week.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards The Patient Aligned Care Team (PACT) Outpatient Staff Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based gender-specific care to primary care patients and oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the setting.

This nurse provides direct Veteran care and care coordination, as it pertains, to Veterans and their care within the Primary Care Department. Manages assigned panel(s), utilizes registries, and ensures appropriate evaluation and access is provided to patient panels.

This nurse provides health promotion, health education and coaching on wellness, disease prevention, and chronic care management. The nurse will assist in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization.

Demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic, primary care through collaborative strategies with others. Evaluates practice in an ongoing process, based on best evidence. Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement.

Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. Contributes professional outpatient nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes.

Supports colleagues through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality outpatient nursing care. Shares educational findings, experiences, and ideas with peers. Questions PACT clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care. Participates in activities and strategies to sustain an evidence-based-practice culture.

Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: To be determined Telework: Not Available Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

The Intensive Community Mental Health Recovery Registered Nurse (ICMHR) assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the MH continuum of care. Follows procedures per established policies and guidelines.

Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team.

MAJOR DUTIES: Promotes personal growth and development of psychiatric-mental health nursing practice. provides clinical community-based case management services to Veterans with pervasive mental illness (PMI), severe functional impairment, and high Inpatient MH unit utilization, in coordination with existing community and Veterans Affairs (VA) services.

Attends and participates in MH interdisciplinary team huddles and meetings, uses therapeutic communication techniques, practices de-escalation techniques, utilizes recovery-oriented language, and provides Veterans, their family members, and/or significant others with education regarding their illness, medications, and treatment plan.

Provides outpatient, community-based mental health services for a subgroup of Veterans with PMI; including but not limited to transportation, medication management, in home/community consultation and responds to psychiatric and medical emergencies as directed.

Documents nursing triage assessments, risk screens, clinical reminders, and patient plan of care in accordance with facility policy. Collaborates and supports mental health nursing along with other disciplines. The ICMHR RN brings principles and theory with limited application of critical thinking skills.
